title: Field notes
intro: Once a week I go through the newsletters I follow on agents, automation and AI tooling and keep the parts a maintenance or operations person could actually use: a sentence or two on the week, then the takeaways, each linked to where it came from.

entries.lede: This week’s thread was quiet failure: agents that stall without erroring, answers that say “nothing found” when nothing was checked, and the growing need to fence what an agent is allowed to touch.

points.t: Make “couldn’t check” a separate result from “checked, found nothing.” Any scheduled report should list the sources it could not reach; a clean zero only counts when every source answered.
Alarm on silence, not only on errors. A loop that only watches flagged items cannot see the one that went quiet; add a “no update in X hours” check, the same idea as flagging a PM nobody has touched.

Before an agent buys, pays or cancels anything: narrow its access, require an explicit approval for each action, and check the result where it lands (the order, the PO), not in the agent’s own summary.
Give each contributor, human or agent, its own folder and protect the main branch. Changes that stay in scope can be approved automatically; anything else gets a review.
Keep shared work in open formats (Markdown, Mermaid diagrams, plain files) so it survives a change of model or vendor.
